surfBiteReport: The most recent available report for this stretch is approximately three weeks old (mid-July 2026). Along the Panama City Beach and adjacent Gulf-front beaches, the surf bite has been steady, particularly during early morning and the last couple of hours before sunset — mid-day heat pushes fish into deeper water or cuts activity sharply. Spanish mackerel, whiting, and redfish are the primary surf-zone targets; mackerel are chasing bait schools close to shore and respond well to spoons and fast-retrieved metals, while whiting are hitting sand fleas, shrimp, and Fishbites fished in the deeper cuts and troughs between sandbars rather than on long-distance casts. Baitfish are thick along the beaches and the predators are following them, so watching for diving birds or jumping bait before picking your spot pays off. Water temperature at this location today is 85°F. No verified current reports (this week) were findable for the 30A corridor specifically (Grayton, Seaside, WaterColor, Inlet Beach), but conditions there typically mirror PCB closely this time of year.
